diagram_candidates.claim: The generators satisfy u_i²=δu_i, adjacent triple relations, distant commutation, and the loop convention assigns δ to a closed component.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source states these local and distant algebra relations together with the loop normalization. A compact cap-cup sketch could connect each relation to its local planar operation.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw the generator as a cap-cup at adjacent positions. Show vertical stacking for e_i², a single closed circle labeled δ; show e_i e_{i+1} e_i=e_i and its mirror; then show two distant generators on disjoint positions commute. Check indices, boundary convention, and loop count against lines 36–50.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: All relations and the loop scalar are explicit in lines 36–50. No defect in the text was found.

diagram_candidates.claim: Paths start at 0, end at vertex a on A_{ℓ−1}, and extend by one adjacent vertex b; the embedding sends E_{p,q}^{(n,a)} to the sum of E_{pb,qb}^{(n+1,b)} over b adjacent to a.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The transition is an adjacency extension and a sum of matrix units over possible next endpoints. A layered path graph can expose branching and direct-sum blocks.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a small A_3 path graph across layers n and n+1, label vertices a and adjacent b, and show each path p ending at a extending to exactly valid pb. Beside it show E_{p,q}^{(n,a)} mapping to the sum over b∼a of E_{pb,qb}^{(n+1,b)}; omit out-of-range endpoints. Check bounds and indices against lines 30–46.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The path constraints and embedding formula are explicit in lines 30–46. No transition-map defect was found.
